\section[Practice]{Review — three jobs, no new words}

\label{lesson:ES-C53-repaso-que}



\begin{quote}
Nothing new. One question first: how many new words did this rung teach you?
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
None. Here is the whole rung:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{Spanish} & \textbf{English} \\
\midrule
joining to a noun & \emph{el libro \textbf{que} compro} & the book that I buy \\
the same, with English's \emph{that} dropped & \emph{la casa \textbf{que} tengo} & the house I have \\
no noun to join to & \emph{\textbf{lo que} digo} & what I say \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\emph{Que} you have held since \emph{quiero que hables}. \emph{Lo} you have held since the object pronouns. This rung put them to work and added nothing.

That is worth pausing on, because it is the last big structural piece a beginner's course owes you, and it turned out to cost \textbf{no vocabulary at all}. Almost everything in a language is like this eventually: the pieces stop being new and start being rearranged.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what to actually watch for}]
One error will outlive the others, so it gets the last word here.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{English deletes its joint. Spanish never does.}
\end{quote}

You will think \emph{the book I bought}, translate what you thought, and produce \emph{el libro compré}. It will feel complete because your English was complete.

The check is mechanical and takes a second: \textbf{a noun, then a new subject and verb, with nothing in between} — that gap needs a \emph{que}.

And when there is no noun to begin with, \emph{lo} supplies one so that \emph{que} has something to hang from. Which means both chapters were about the same thing: \textbf{Spanish will not let the joint go missing.}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} all three rows of the table
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:} Until the missing English \emph{that} is loud.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
New words this rung? (\textbf{None}.) The error that outlives the others? (\textbf{Dropping \emph{que}}, because English drops \emph{that}.) Next: sentences long enough to be worth saying.
\end{tcolorbox}
